ideas.title: A motor fitted by hand that runs because the field pushes it
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: This is the big goal's core, and the island has never had it. The player assembles a motor from parts, and the commutation, the dead spot, the running backwards and the sparks all come from contact and field solves. It is a mechanic, not another three-variant study. The risk is scope: if the circuit solve or the commutator contact gets faked into a rig for one setup, it falls back to a scripted spin, and then it is the homopolar wire again.

ideas.title: A cart that drives because its parts do
ideas.critique: This is the payoff the big goal is for, but its first step is a hand-pushed cart rolling on the terrain. Players will read that as one more rolling prop, and the motor it depends on does not exist yet. Its strength (load sag, stalling on the dune, friends adding mass) only shows once the motor and the cells are real, so taken now it is mostly a wheeled body.

ideas.title: Static in Truffle's fur
ideas.critique: Charged fur rising strand by strand and a spark that depends on the gap and the nose is new physics on a creature. It is playful: you sneak up on friends, and it comes out different each time. A few hundred strands plus a boundary-element solve on moving bodies is a lot, and it is easy to fudge with a fitted charge per stroke. For the cart it only touches the theme of charge and contact.

ideas.title: Sparks off the grindstone tell you the metal
ideas.critique: The spark particles burst by their carbon, with Planck colour as emissive trails, and that makes a beautiful traced night shot of a kind the island has not filmed. As play it is a lookup: hold a lump to the wheel, read the answer, and after one go each you know them all. The link to the cart is only that the materials table gets used.

ideas.title: A cell in a clam shell lifts the crane
ideas.critique: It builds the circuit solver and the cell, which are two road steps, and gives the coil crane a current nobody set, so it is a real step. What players see is the same crane dipping into the same spikes, now lifting more. The film's payoff (pegs come up) is what 'A coil on a cord' already promised, so the wow has to come from wiring the shells up and watching it fail.

ideas.title: Bellows and green rock: the first copper bead
ideas.critique: A hopping rhythm against a real heat balance is a proper game, and a night kiln mouth glowing by its own temperature is good material for the path tracer. Reduction above fixed temperature thresholds and copper running down by gravity are likely to come out as thresholds on one number. It is the last road step, done before anything needs copper made on the island.

ideas.title: A hot wire in dry grass
ideas.critique: The glowing wire by Joule and Planck is new, but most of the film is grass catching and fire spreading downwind, which the campfire just showed. Without the circuit solver it has to set a current by hand, and then it is a heater on a timer.

ideas.title: Turn the potter's wheel and the wire glows
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: The back torque the player feels when the wire is shorted is the strong, rarely simulated bit: an interaction that pushes back, not a visual. It needs the circuit solve to be honest, and with one stone over one coil on one axis it risks being a rig for one setup.

ideas.title: Wire through the draw plate
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
same_form: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: It reuses wire.jl's hardening as a craft with a real fail state (the snap) and a fix (annealing), and Lumi braced and hauling is good character animation. It has the same shape as the bent-wire post, though: a tool works copper and its simulated state changes. It is also an area reduction per hole with a strength check, not a flow simulation.

ideas.title: A buzzer that sings by breaking its own circuit
ideas.critique: A self-oscillating circuit whose pitch and waveform come out of the beam, the field and L/R would be a first: a machine part you hear, with sound from real motion. It proves out contact-made circuits, which the commutator needs. As play it is retune-and-listen, and the conga is a scripted garnish.
